transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-09-09
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Alex Martinez (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Head of Search, BrightMart), Maya Patel (ML Eng), Jon Rivera (Product)

Summary (auto): quick demo of embeddings + rerank, show Console traces, discuss pilot and SSO/security.

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood Inference, with Priya on the line, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Liam: Good, thanks. Excited to see how this can help our site search, we've been hitting a plateau with our current vector pipeline.
[00:12] Priya: Great, we'll focus on embeddings first, then the rerank endpoint and a live example of search relevance. Note: we'll show hosted API flows, not dedicated right now, but we can switch topics.
[00:22] Maya: Quick FYI - we care about latency under 120ms p50 and costs; also SOC 2 + SSO is a must.
[00:29] Alex: Totally, we'll touch on those. Ok Priya go ahead.

[02:10] Priya: Alright so here's the Redwood Console, this is the Hosted API experience. You can see model catalog, embeddings endpoint, and example payloads. For BrightMart I'd recommend starting with our re-embedding profile tuned for retail catalogs.
[02:33] (Priya shares screen: console.redwood.ai/demo)
[02:45] Priya: Example request: POST /v1/embeddings with a small batch of product descriptions. We return dense vectors; for rerank we call the rerank endpoint with candidate ids + query embedding.
[03:12] Jon: Ping me on the format - is it ID + vector or do you expect full text?
[03:18] Priya: Good q. The rerank endpoint accepts an array of candidates where you can pass either the text or the precomputed vector id. If you have an existing vector store like Pinecone or Milvus you can keep them and send top-K ids and their vectors; Redwood can accept either.
[03:40] Liam: About relevance - we do a two-stage flow: ANN fetch + rerank. We want to see lift vs just ANN.
[03:47] Priya: Exactly. We'll show an example: ANN from your vector DB (we simulated), then call Redwood rerank which uses the query and candidate contexts to produce a score and optionally an explanation. The rerank model is cheaper than doing full generation but gives improved ordering.
[04:10] (brief crosstalk)

[06:05] Priya: Demo time - I'll send a sample query "blue waterproof hiking jacket" and 5 product candidates. First run: baseline ANN ordering, then call rerank.
[06:18] (typing noises)
[06:25] Priya: Baseline API call to embeddings... the payloads are slightly noisy in the transcript here, sometimes the console autopopulated.
[06:40] Priya: Baseline ANN top 5: Candidate IDs 113, 78, 204, 19, 350. Rerank call in 60ms on hosted endpoint, returned reordered list with 78, 113, 19, 350, 204 and higher score for 78 which matched the long-tail attributes (waterproof rating).
[07:05] Maya: That's a big win — we see problems where user intent around attributes isn't captured by pure vector distance. How tunable is rerank?
[07:13] Priya: You can feed additional context like product attributes, session signals; Redwood Optimize can suggest feature weights and sampling strategies. Also you can set fallback policies if latency spikes.
[07:25] Alex: On cost — rerank is priced per candidate scored plus a base request; our pricing sheet will show examples. Typically two-stage (ANN + rerank on top-k 5-20) balances cost and quality.

[09:00] Liam: Latency numbers? We need p95 under 250ms for search page.
[09:07] Priya: For hosted endpoints, we often see ~30-120ms p50 for rerank at k=10, p95 can be 150-300ms depending on payload size and model; we can tune model variant and batching. We also have prefix/KV caching for repeated queries which helps.
[09:24] Jon: What about regional routing — our traffic is US + EU?
[09:29] Alex: Hosted supports regional routing, or Dedicated/Private for strict residency. We can pin a model version and route EU traffic to EU region to satisfy data locality.

[11:40] Priya: I'll show the API snippet for rerank and how we include candidate metadata. (shares code) POST /v1/rerank { query: "...", candidates: [{id: "113", text: "...", metadata: {category: "jacket"}}, ...] } Response includes scores and rationale.
[12:10] Maya: Is the rationale deterministic? We need stable ordering for A/B tests.
[12:16] Priya: Rerank is deterministic for a given model version and inputs; randomness only if you enable sampling in certain models for exploration. You can lock model version.

[14:00] Liam: Security checklist - do you retain raw text? Are calls logged?
[14:06] Alex: Hosted defaults to short retention for telemetry, but for enterprise we can toggle retention and integrate with your KMS/HSM. We have SOC 2, ISO references. We'll share the security packet.
[14:20] Maya: We require SSO/SAML and RBAC - doable?
[14:23] Alex: Yes — SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning, per-route RBAC are supported on our Console and Dedicated/Private.

[17:00] Priya: Back to relevance — here's a before/after on a sample query set. We measured MRR improvement ~12% on our retail bench when using rerank on top-10. I pulled a quick spreadsheet and will include it. (mentions shared link: drive.redwood/demo/brightmart-relevance)
[17:30] Jon: Nice — can you run that on our data quickly?
[17:34] Priya: We can — pilot is easiest: you give us a small dataset (anonymized) and we run a hosted benchmark with representative queries; that takes ~1-2 business days to get initial results.

[20:15] (discussion: integration path)
[20:40] Alex: Integration options: 1) keep your vector DB and call rerank on top-K, 2) migrate embeddings into Redwood-managed vector store, or 3) full Dedicated with private network. For BrightMart, option 1 is lowest friction.
[21:00] Liam: We're leaning that route. We also want to measure cost for steady-state traffic ~200 qps.
[21:10] Alex: We'll model that in the pricing sheet — include batching, k, and cache hit rates.

[24:00] Maya: Any gotchas on content filters or PII redaction?
[24:06] Priya: Redwood's hosted API has filters and you can request no retention; for regulated data Dedicated/Private recommended. We'll flag this in the security doc.

[26:30] Priya: Quick look at Console logs — you can see token breakdown, latency by model and route, and per-request metadata. Very helpful for debugging regressions.
[27:05] Jon: Do you have evaluation tooling to run prompt-based checks?
[27:12] Priya: Yes, Redwood Optimize includes evaluation harness, prompt sets, regression alerts. We can attach your golden queries to monitor quality over model updates.

[30:00] (brief pause while sharing artifacts)
[31:10] Alex: A couple of notes on SLA — Hosted has best-effort with usage commitments possible; Dedicated includes SLA-backed uptime and latency tiers.
[31:30] Liam: We might start hosted for speed then evaluate Dedicated if we need more guarantees.

[33:00] Priya: Demo wrap-up: rerank example again with different k values to show tradeoffs. k=5 gave p50 45ms, k=20 p50 90ms but improved recall slightly.
[34:00] Maya: Sounds good. We'll want to run ablations on attribute-aware scoring.

[36:15] Jon: Any integrations or SDKs we should use?
[36:20] Priya: We have Python/Node SDKs and examples for vector store connectors. I'll share sample code for Pinecone and Milvus adapters.

[38:40] Alex: Ok let's recap next steps. I'll email the pricing/benchmark spreadsheet and the security packet; Priya will share the rerank notebook and quickstart snippets. We agreed to plan a 1-week pilot after BrightMart shares anonymized dataset and query logs.
[39:05] Liam: Timeline: we'll aim to decide by next Friday and get dataset by the following Monday.
[39:20] Alex: Great. Anything else?
[39:25] Maya: One more — can you include a sample p95 latency report for traffic at 200 qps?
[39:30] Priya: Yes, will include that in the benchmark sheet.

[41:00] (closing pleasantries)
[41:10] Alex: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts.
[41:15] Liam: Thanks.

End of recording. Some transcription noise: product names sometimes mis-heard (e.g. "KV cache" became "K V case"), timestamps approximate.
